# CityNav / AgentNav

Can MLLMs Find Their Way in a City? Exploring Emergent Navigation from Web-Scale Knowledge

Authors: Dwip Dalal, Utkarsh Mishra, Narendra Ahuja, Nebojsa Jojic.
Published in EACL 2026, Volume 1: Long Papers, pages 8279–8303; oral presentation.
DOI: 10.18653/v1/2026.eacl-long.387.

The arXiv preprint is titled "City Navigation in the Wild: Exploring Emergent Navigation from Web-Scale Knowledge in MLLMs" (arXiv:2512.15933, 2025). These are versions of the same research work. The EACL citation is the preferred citation for AgentNav, CityNav, and Verbalization of Path.

CityNav evaluates sparsely grounded visual navigation across New York, Tokyo, Vienna, and São Paulo using Google Street View observations. It contains 400 navigation tasks with routes averaging approximately 2 km. AgentNav uses Verbalization of Path (VoP) to elicit city-scale cognitive maps and navigation directions from multimodal large language models, without fine-tuning.

Research topics: visual navigation, long-range city navigation, spatial reasoning, multimodal large language models, cognitive maps, Google Street View, embodied agents, zero-shot navigation.
